## Profile

Health economist specialising in the economic evaluation of health technologies
alongside clinical trials and in methods for health technology assessment, with
a background in applied statistics and psychology. Experienced in communicating
analyses to both technical and non-technical audiences.

## Experience

[Jan 2023–present]{.cv-date} **Research Fellow in Pharmacoeconomics**, Centre
for Health Economics and Medicines Evaluation (CHEME), Bangor University

[May 2021–Dec 2022]{.cv-date} **Research Officer in Health Technology
Assessment**, CHEME, Bangor University

[Nov 2020–Mar 2021]{.cv-date} **Research Officer in Pharmacoepidemiology**,
CHEME, Bangor University

- Project: the scale and variation of the impact of COVID-19 on prescribing of
  medicines in primary care in Wales
  - Responsible for creating an analytical strategy for identifying changes to
    primary-care prescribing in Wales during the COVID-19 pandemic and for
    disseminating the results
  - Project documented at <https://github.com/w-hardy/sercymru>
  - Package created for the analysis: <https://github.com/w-hardy/serCymruTools>

[2018–present]{.cv-date} **Research Consultant**

I have worked as a research consultant for several organisations, conducting
both quantitative and qualitative research. Examples include:

- Quantitative / data science
  - Development of elite performance in elite sport and high-performance
    business (e.g., England and Wales Cricket Board, Watford FC, OSTC group)
    - Responsible for data collation (including biometric, survey, performance
      and trial data) and creating individual profiling reports (using R
      Markdown), used by both technical (e.g., performance psychologists) and
      non-technical audiences (e.g., coaches)
    - Worked as part of a group of performance psychologists working with
      performers and their coaches
  - North Sea oil and gas COVID-19 repatriation (Outreach Medic Skills Ltd. and
    Bristow Helicopters)
    - Designed and implemented a data collection and automated reporting system
      to provide insights into their COVID-19 medevac service
  - An evaluation of the Adverse Childhood Experience Trauma Informed
    Multi-Agency Early Action Together (ACE TIME) training: national roll-out
    to police and partners (Public Health Wales)
    - Responsible for quality assurance of the analyses and findings reported
- Qualitative
  - Analysis of "Situational Analysis" and "Sporting and Organisational Health"
    documents (UK Sport)
    - Responsible for the entire project, including analysis of documents
      submitted by Olympic and Paralympic sports (approximately 40 sports,
      ~1,500 pages) and report writing, on a very short timeline in April 2020
  - Perceptions of healthy ageing (NRS Healthcare)
    - Responsible for study design, analysing focus-group data, report writing
      and presenting findings

## Skills

**Health economics**: trial-based cost-effectiveness analysis, decision
modelling, probabilistic sensitivity analysis, survival extrapolation (including
cure and spline models), value of information.

**Applied statistics**: Bayesian and frequentist analysis, generalised linear
models, pattern recognition / machine learning, structural equation modelling,
multilevel / random-effects modelling, time-series analysis, survival analysis,
Monte Carlo simulation, cluster analysis.

**Computing**: R/RStudio\*, Git, SQL, Mplus\*, Python†, MS Office\*, NVivo,
LaTeX, SPSS, JASP (\*highly skilled, †basic knowledge, others to a competent
level).
